holidays.name: National Green Bean Casserole Day
holidays.description: A salute to the creamy, crunchy, mushroom-soupy side dish that has a permanent spot on American holiday tables. Celebrate by baking one, topped with a heap of crispy fried onions, and pretending it counts as a vegetable.
holidays.origin: The dish was created in 1955 by Dorcas Reilly, a home economist at the Campbell Soup Company, who developed it for a recipe feature. It was meant to be quick and made from pantry staples, and it became a holiday classic.
holidays.funFact: Dorcas Reilly's original recipe card is kept in the archives of the Campbell Soup Company, and her recipe is still made by millions of families every year.

holidays.name: National Roof Over Your Head Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate having shelter and to help people who don't. You could volunteer for a home-building project, donate to a shelter, or just give your ceiling a grateful look.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is widely listed on the December calendar as a reminder to be thankful for a safe place to live during the holiday season.
holidays.funFact: Nobody knows who started it, but it fits well with the season, since many charities run shelter and home-repair drives in early December.

holidays.name: Make a Gift Day
holidays.description: A holiday that asks you to skip the shopping mall and make a present by hand. Knit it, bake it, paint it, or glue-gun it, because the lopsided homemade gift is the one people remember.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It appears to have started as a nudge toward handmade, thoughtful gift-giving in the run-up to the December holidays.
holidays.funFact: Handmade gifts have a name among psychologists: studies on the "IKEA effect" suggest people value things more when they put effort into making them.
